title: Soft Threshold Handoff Worksheet & Week Calendar — draft
content:
Purpose:
This is a working handoff and week-level calendar for the "soft threshold" rollout experiment. The aim is to exercise staggered traffic thresholds and progressive KV-cache warmup while minimizing user-visible regressions. Treat this as the single source for on-call and release leads during the 7-day window; copy relevant sections into the launch Slack channel and pager handover.

Summary of approach:
- Soft threshold = we shift traffic by small increments to a new model variant/quantization profile but keep the old variant available as a fallback.
- Staggered lanes (A/B/C) for region and customer-tier separation.
- Primary goals: 95th p99 token latency <= 220ms (hosted), error-rate delta < +0.3% compared to baseline, no QoE regressions on canonical eval set.

Success criteria (must be green for +24h before broadening):
- Latency SLO: 95th <= 220ms (hosted API) and 99th <= 400ms for dedicated pools.
- Error budget: < +0.3% increase in 5xx + user-facing errors vs last 7-day baseline.
- Quality: No >1.5% drop in prompt-set pass-rate for golden evals (regression tests).
- Resource: GPU utilization steady; no >2x jump in token cost.

Week calendar (high-level) — June 7–13, 2027:
- Tue 07 Jun — Preflight window: infra checks, canary image bake, config push to canary lane. (09:00–12:00 PDT)
- Tue 07 Jun — Canary open (lane A): 1% traffic. Watch for 4 hours.
- Tue 07 Jun — Expand lane A to 5% if green (14:00 PDT)
- Wed 08 Jun — Lane B (regional group): start 1% -> 5% after 6h
- Thu 09 Jun — Ramp lane A/B to 10% combined if all checks pass
- Fri 10 Jun — Weekend watch: hold at safe threshold 10–15% through Sat. Internal-only telemetry sampling increased.
- Mon 13 Jun — Decision window: full rollout OR rollback. If green for 72h, plan full ramp next Tue with ops-runbook.

Preflight checklist (owners assigned):
- Infra / Deployment (Owen Chen):
  - Confirm canary images built and signed (GH PR #723).
  - Verify config replication to dedicated capacity groups.
  - Load test baseline against a shadow cluster (target QPS +20%).

- Telemetry / Observability (Priya Nair):
  - Confirm synthetic traffic for top-20 prompts is instrumented.
  - Ensure alert rules are enabled for p95/p99 latency and token generation errors.
  - Validate logging: trace IDs propagate through gateway -> runtime -> model host.

- QA / Eval (Leah Kim):
  - Run golden prompt set (regression harness) and record pass-rate.
  - Smoke test long-context sessions (4k tokens) and short-dialog flows.

- SRE / Oncall (SRE shift lead):
  - Pager rotations confirmed for 24/7 with escalation path.
  - Slack channel created: #launch-soft-threshold (pin runbook link).

Stagger strategy (detailed):
- Lane A (global low-risk customers) — initial 1% -> 5% -> 10% over 48h
- Lane B (regional EU customers) — start after lane A stable, 1% -> 5%
- Lane C (internal & staging) — traffic mirrored throughout for KV warm cache
- If global spike or latency > threshold:
  - Immediately cut lane A/B to previous model variant (automatic fallback).
  - Notify release lead and SRE in Slack and page if 15m sustained breach.

Telemetry watchlist + thresholds (alerts to trigger review):
- p95 latency (generation): threshold 220ms — page if 15m above
- p99 latency: threshold 400ms — page if 10m sustained
- Error-rate (generated 5xx + runtime errors): >0.3% increase vs baseline — alert
- Token dropouts (incomplete responses): any >0.05% and trending upward 30m — investigate
- Throttles / backpressure: any queueing >10s — immediate action

Rollback & mitigation plan:
- Soft rollback: switch traffic routing policy to previous model variant (2min rollout).
- Hard rollback: scale down new pools and re-enable old pools; begin postmortem trigger.
- Communication: use release channel and post an incident stub in Confluence.

Release notes draft (to be refined for customer-facing):
- New rollout: soft-threshold rollout of model-v2-quantized across select customers to validate latency/cost profile.
- Impact: No expected user-visible changes. Improvements: ~20% lower per-token cost on long-context queries in lab tests.
- Known limitations: small flicker in latency under high concurrency; will monitor.

Open questions / action items (quick):
- Q1: Should we enable aggressive prefix caching for lane B now or wait until lane A shows stable KV warmup? (owner: Leah; JIRA:RELEASE-9124)
- Q2: Do we add an additional canary metric for end-to-end user-perceived latency using the browser synthetic? (owner: Priya)
- Q3: Confirm legal/privacy signoff for EU region telemetry retention adjustments. (owner: Owen)

Quick links and artifacts:
- PR with canary config: https://github.com/redwood-inference/service-config/pull/723
- Deployment playbook (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RE/Soft+Threshold+Playbook
- Primary ticket: JIRA RELEASE-9124

Immediate next steps (today):
1) Owen: finalize image signing + post commit artifact in #launch-soft-threshold (ETA: EOD Tue).
2) Priya: enable extra synthetic sampling and verify alerts (ETA: 09:00 Tue).
3) Leah: run golden eval and attach results to JIRA (ETA: noon Tue).

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the A/B splits tiny at first; we want to see signal not noise.
- If telemetry is noisy, add sampled traces for requests hitting the new variant (not all users).
- Document any manual steps we do in the Slack thread so runbook can be updated post-launch.

Revision log:
- 2027-06-01 Leah Kim: initial draft and checklist
- 2027-06-07 Owen Chen: added infra gating steps and PR link
- 2027-06-10 Priya Nair: expanded telemetry watchlist and thresholds

(End of doc)
